We know that value is top of mind for consumers, and Dealworthy, backed by our owned brand promise, will not only appeal to our current guests but position us to attract even more new shoppers to Target,” said Rick Gomez, Target chief food, essentials and beauty officer.

*   In most cases, the threat of an Amazon Private Label brand dominating a given category has passed 
    *   For a number of years, Amazon Private Label was viewed as a sort of boogeyman by brands, with the knowledge that if they entered your market it was incredibly hard to compete with them across a range of areas
    *   This latest analysis makes it clear that Amazon’s Private Label revenues are declining across a majority of categories
    *   Amazon’s current private label catalog is largely centered around less differentiated goods (e.g. basic collared shirts, basic exercise equipment, baby essentials, etc.) rather than more niche product varieties 
        *   With this in mind, even for brands still competing against Amazon Private Label, you can effectively differentiate your products from a marketing and content perspective by focusing on a product’s quality, unique features, and use cases

After years of brands and legislators alike [**expressing their concerns**](https://www.wsj.com/articles/amazon-to-meet-with-ftc-officials-ahead-of-expected-antitrust-complaint-fbb0927f?mod=article_inline) around Amazon Private Label brands, an analysis of Q1 sales and badging activity shows that Amazon’s [**pullback in this area that began in earnest in 2023**](https://www.wsj.com/articles/amazon-cuts-dozens-of-house-brands-as-it-battles-costs-regulators-3f6ad56d?mod=djemalertNEWS) is truly starting to express itself in the marketplace. Overall, Amazon Private Label sales reached more than $1B in Q1 2024 – roughly the size of Samsung on the site. However, between Q1 2023 and Q1 2024, the collective share of Amazon US retail revenue going to the retailer’s private label brands shrunk from 1.0% to 0.9%, with declines occurring across 16 of the top 20 physical goods categories.

*   Category dynamics around search-specific badges have changed markedly 
    *   [**Just two years ago, Amazon’s Private Label brands captured large shares of Amazon’s Choice badges**](https://www.momentumcommerce.com/amazon-choice-badge-private-label/) across a number of categories – those numbers have dropped precipitously
    *   This waning influence of Amazon’s Private Label brands – which tended to be lower priced and optimized for search visibility – opens up a clearer path to attaining an ‘Overall Pick’ badge across a wide range of search terms 
        *   Achieving faster sales velocity through paid and organic means should be a focus here, as these badges are likely awarded based on some combination of price, sales history, reviews, and relevance.

When you buy Kirkland batteries at Costco, you're purchasing a private label product. Costco doesn't manufacture, but it works with a manufacturer to produce batteries under the Kirkland Signature brand.

US private label sales [**hit $271 billion in 2024**](https://customcy.com/blog/private-label-statistics/) and continue growing faster than national brands. Over half of Amazon sellers use the private label model. The majority become profitable within their first year.

# 2 0 2 4Dear Shareholders: 2024 was a strong year for Amazon. Our total revenue grew 11% year-over-year (“YoY”) from $575B to $638B. By segment, North America revenue increased 10% YoY from $353B to $387B, International revenue grew 9% YoY from $131B to $143B, and AWS revenue increased 19% YoY, from $91B to $108B. For perspective, just 10 years ago, AWS revenue was $4.6B; and in that same year, Amazon’s total revenue was $89B. Amazon’s operating income in 2024 improved 86% YoY, from $36.9B (an operating margin of 6.4%) to $68.6B (an operating margin of 10.8%). Free Cash Flow, adjusted for equipment finance leases improved from $35.5B in 2023 to $36.2B. Apart from the financial results, we made our customers’ lives meaningfully better and easier. In our Stores business, we substantially expanded selection, continued lowering prices (independent research firm, Profitero, found Amazon the lowest-priced online U.S.

Retailer for the eighth year in a row), and for the second year in a row, we shipped at record speed to our Prime members. AWS launched a slew of new infrastructure and AI services that make it even easier to build remarkable customer experiences, including our latest custom AI silicon (Trainium2), a new set of frontier foundation models in Amazon Nova, and significant expansion of available models and features in our leading Generative AI (“GenAI”) services Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock. Prime Video continued to offer compelling original shows, including new seasons for Fallout, Reacher, The Boys, and The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power , movies like

Road House, The Idea of You, and Red One , live sports like Thursday Night Football and UEFA Champions League in Europe (with the NBA and NASCAR coming in 2025), and new selection, highlighted by Apple TV+ joining Prime Video Channels. We launched a series of new Kindle devices that included a new color version, a larger Scribe option, and our fastest Paperwhites ever (the collection of which drove the highest Kindle unit sales for a single quarter in over a decade). And, we continued to add more selection, price transparency, and same day shipping for Amazon Pharmacy. These accomplishments are a subset of what the team launched in 2024, but represent a lot of invention, hard work, and thoughtful execution across Amazon. I’m thankful for my teammates and their delivery this past year (some of which you can see in our 2024 results, others of which won’t be visible for the next few years).

Every year in my annual letter, I try to share insight into what makes Amazon tick. At the highest level, we’re aiming to be Earth’s most customer-centric company, making customers’ lives better and easier every day. This is not easy to do in general, let alone year after year. In fact, it’s actually quite hard, especially with the rapid rate of change in technology, customer habits, and new products from large and small companies alike. If we want to have a chance at succeeding in our mission, we have to constantly question everything around us. We’ve had this long-held philosophy at Amazon about two-way and one-way door decisions. A two-way door decision is one where if you get the decision wrong, you can walk back through that door, revert to where you were, and there are few (if any) ramifications. # 2 0 2 4Dear Shareholders: 2024 was a strong year for Amazon. Our total revenue grew 11% year-over-year (“YoY”) from $575B to $638B. By segment, North America revenue increased 10% YoY from $353B to $387B, International revenue grew 9% YoY from $131B to $143B, and AWS revenue increased 19% YoY, from $91B to $108B. For perspective, just 10 years ago, AWS revenue was $4.6B; and in that same year, Amazon’s total revenue was $89B. Amazon’s operating income in 2024 improved 86% YoY, from $36.9B (an operating margin of 6.4%) to $68.6B (an operating margin of 10.8%). Free Cash Flow, adjusted for equipment finance leases improved from $35.5B in 2023 to $36.2B. Apart from the financial results, we made our customers’ lives meaningfully better and easier. In our Stores business, we substantially expanded selection, continued lowering prices (independent research firm, Profitero, found Amazon the lowest-priced online U.S.

Retailer for the eighth year in a row), and for the second year in a row, we shipped at record speed to our Prime members. AWS launched a slew of new infrastructure and AI services that make it even easier to build remarkable customer experiences, including our latest custom AI silicon (Trainium2), a new set of frontier foundation models in Amazon Nova, and significant expansion of available models and features in our leading Generative AI (“GenAI”) services Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock. Prime Video continued to offer compelling original shows, including new seasons for Fallout, Reacher, The Boys, and The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power , movies like

Road House, The Idea of You, and Red One , live sports like Thursday Night Football and UEFA Champions League in Europe (with the NBA and NASCAR coming in 2025), and new selection, highlighted by Apple TV+ joining Prime Video Channels. We launched a series of new Kindle devices that included a new color version, a larger Scribe option, and our fastest Paperwhites ever (the collection of which drove the highest Kindle unit sales for a single quarter in over a decade). And, we continued to add more selection, price transparency, and same day shipping for Amazon Pharmacy. These accomplishments are a subset of what the team launched in 2024, but represent a lot of invention, hard work, and thoughtful execution across Amazon. I’m thankful for my teammates and their delivery this past year (some of which you can see in our 2024 results, others of which won’t be visible for the next few years).

Every year in my annual letter, I try to share insight into what makes Amazon tick. At the highest level, we’re aiming to be Earth’s most customer-centric company, making customers’ lives better and easier every day. This is not easy to do in general, let alone year after year. In fact, it’s actually quite hard, especially with the rapid rate of change in technology, customer habits, and new products from large and small companies alike. If we want to have a chance at succeeding in our mission, we have to constantly question everything around us. We’ve had this long-held philosophy at Amazon about two-way and one-way door decisions. A two-way door decision is one where if you get the decision wrong, you can walk back through that door, revert to where you were, and there are few (if any) ramifications. You can make these decisions quickly and locally.

Advertising services are becoming increasingly important as Amazon finds new ways to sell digital ad spots to businesses on its website and through its streaming platforms like Prime and Twitch. In Q3, advertising services revenue grew by 25% year over year, the fastest pace of any segment.

The third-party marketplace has been the primary driver of this [ongoing transformation](https://www.marketplacepulse.com/articles/amazons-evolution-to-retail-infrastructure-provider), with seller services generating $42.5 billion in Q3 alone. Sellers now account for [62% of units sold on Amazon](https://www.marketplacepulse.com/stats/amazon-percent-of-units-by-third-party-sellers), and Amazon collects [roughly 50% of their revenue](https://www.marketplacepulse.com/articles/amazon-takes-a-50-cut-of-sellers-revenue) through various fees. Amazon’s quietly accelerating B2B offering, Amazon Business, [had a $35 billion annual run rate when last reported in 2023](https://www.marketplacepulse.com/articles/amazons-35-billion-b2b-marketplace), and is now likely over $50 billion, representing a not-insignificant share of total GMV.

In Q3 2025, the company generated $73 billion from combined online and physical store sales, while its service businesses – third-party seller fees, advertising, subscriptions, AWS, and its ‘others’ category – delivered $107 billion. It’s a trajectory that has been consistent for years, but the milestone is nonetheless significant: 60% and rising of Amazon is now providing services rather than selling products.
Amazon’s retail business now accounts for just 40.5% of the company’s total revenue, marking a new milestone in its evolution from an online bookstore to a commerce infrastructure provider.

Interesting data. Couple of thoughts. 1. If rogue 3P sellers are harming your revenue and EBITDA then prepare for it to get worse. 3P sellers (and 1P for that matter) are growing 9% YOY. 2. Amazon is not incentivized to inhibit rogue sellers as they are a key growth lever. 3. The US is still Amazon's fuel as it represents 53% of worldwide GMV. 4. Amazon competes simultaneously on price, speed, and discovery which drives rogue sellers to (mis?)behave the same way. Buy box control is essential to ecommerce professionals maximize revenue and EBITDA. (Want to guess who can help with this one??) 5. How does Walmart's $1T market cap influence Amazon (if at all)? What are your takeaways from the article? [https://lnkd.in/gU-WVgnu](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Flnkd%2Ein%2FgU-WVgnu&urlhash=KlUw&trk=public_post-text)

Amazon isn’t slowing down. It’s entrenching itself. After yesterday’s earnings call everyone was shocked to learn how Amazon is planning to invest at a scale no other retail platform can match. For 2026 Amazon plans to spend ~$200B in CAPEX, largely on AI, logistics, and automation. That investment supports a business that now moves an estimated $830B in global GMV (nearly 3× more than seven years ago). According to Marketplace Pulse: $255B from Amazon retail (1P) $575B from third-party sellers (3P) Both growing ~9% YoY Underneath is a structural shift: Third-party sellers generate 69% of GMV, yet only ~62% of units. Amazon keeps high-volume, low-price essentials. The marketplace handles higher-value, branded goods.

[![Image 6: Amazon GMV Surpassed $800 Billion in 2025](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/joshuaabenson_amazon-gmv-surpassed-800-billion-in-2025-activity-7425562812313395200-bGio) Amazon GMV Surpassed $800 Billion in 2025 marketplacepulse.com](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww%2Emarketplacepulse%2Ecom%2Farticles%2Famazon-gmv-surpassed-800-billion-in-2025&urlhash=IjV5&trk=public_post_feed-article-content)

[Amazon](https://www.linkedin.com/company/amazon?trk=public_post-text) GMV surpassing $800 billion isn’t just a milestone — it’s a signal that the platform has evolved from an e-commerce retailer into one of the most powerful commercial infrastructures in the world. According to [Marketplace Pulse](https://www.linkedin.com/company/marketplace-pulse?trk=public_post-text), Amazon’s scale today reflects a marketplace increasingly dominated by sophisticated operators rather than casual sellers. Growth isn’t just about more participants — it’s about bigger, more capable brands leveraging logistics, advertising, and data at scale. 👉 What stands out to me is how the narrative around Amazon is shifting: First, GMV growth continues even as seller entry slows. New seller registrations hit a decade low in 2025, suggesting Amazon is becoming less of an entrepreneurial playground and more of a performance-driven ecosystem built for serious operators.

The third-party marketplace remains the primary growth engine, though its expansion has moderated. Since 2019, sales on Amazon have grown by an estimated $495 billion, with the marketplace responsible for roughly 76% of that incremental GMV. The steady shift from first-party to third-party sales continues – sellers now represent 69% of total GMV, up from 60% in 2019 – but the pace has slowed from the [150 basis points annually](https://www.marketplacepulse.com/articles/amazon-sales-top-700-billion-in-2023) that characterized the prior decade to just 20 basis points in 2025.

The deceleration becomes clearer when examining unit share rather than GMV share. Third-party sellers’ portion of total units sold has [plateaued at 61-62%](https://www.marketplacepulse.com/stats/amazon-percent-of-units-by-third-party-sellers) for five consecutive quarters, even as their GMV share continued climbing to 69%. This divergence reveals Amazon’s strategic positioning: the company retains control of high-volume, low-price categories – consumables, basics, private label products – while the marketplace handles higher-value goods. Amazon retail generates more transactions but less revenue per unit, while marketplace sellers command better prices on specialized products and branded items. raw_passages.text: # 2 0 2 4Dear Shareholders: 2024 was a strong year for Amazon. Our total revenue grew 11% year-over-year (“YoY”) from $575B to $638B. By segment, North America revenue increased 10% YoY from $353B to $387B, International revenue grew 9% YoY from $131B to $143B, and AWS revenue increased 19% YoY, from $91B to $108B. For perspective, just 10 years ago, AWS revenue was $4.6B; and in that same year, Amazon’s total revenue was $89B. Amazon’s operating income in 2024 improved 86% YoY, from $36.9B (an operating margin of 6.4%) to $68.6B (an operating margin of 10.8%). Free Cash Flow, adjusted for equipment finance leases improved from $35.5B in 2023 to $36.2B. Apart from the financial results, we made our customers’ lives meaningfully better and easier. In our Stores business, we substantially expanded selection, continued lowering prices (independent research firm, Profitero, found Amazon the lowest-priced online U.S.

Retailer for the eighth year in a row), and for the second year in a row, we shipped at record speed to our Prime members. AWS launched a slew of new infrastructure and AI services that make it even easier to build remarkable customer experiences, including our latest custom AI silicon (Trainium2), a new set of frontier foundation models in Amazon Nova, and significant expansion of available models and features in our leading Generative AI (“GenAI”) services Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock. Prime Video continued to offer compelling original shows, including new seasons for Fallout, Reacher, The Boys, and The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power , movies like

Road House, The Idea of You, and Red One , live sports like Thursday Night Football and UEFA Champions League in Europe (with the NBA and NASCAR coming in 2025), and new selection, highlighted by Apple TV+ joining Prime Video Channels. We launched a series of new Kindle devices that included a new color version, a larger Scribe option, and our fastest Paperwhites ever (the collection of which drove the highest Kindle unit sales for a single quarter in over a decade). And, we continued to add more selection, price transparency, and same day shipping for Amazon Pharmacy. These accomplishments are a subset of what the team launched in 2024, but represent a lot of invention, hard work, and thoughtful execution across Amazon. I’m thankful for my teammates and their delivery this past year (some of which you can see in our 2024 results, others of which won’t be visible for the next few years).

Every year in my annual letter, I try to share insight into what makes Amazon tick. At the highest level, we’re aiming to be Earth’s most customer-centric company, making customers’ lives better and easier every day. This is not easy to do in general, let alone year after year. In fact, it’s actually quite hard, especially with the rapid rate of change in technology, customer habits, and new products from large and small companies alike. If we want to have a chance at succeeding in our mission, we have to constantly question everything around us. We’ve had this long-held philosophy at Amazon about two-way and one-way door decisions. A two-way door decision is one where if you get the decision wrong, you can walk back through that door, revert to where you were, and there are few (if any) ramifications. You can make these decisions quickly and locally.

CFO Brian Olsavsky underscored this shift during the Q1 2025 earnings call , declaring inventory placement as Amazon’s number one operational priority . The restructured inbound network allows a greater share of products to be positioned more strategically within fulfillment centers, resulting in: Record-breaking delivery speeds globally for Prime members Highest-ever volume of same-day and next-day deliveries in a single quarter Lower delivery costs, supported by improved unit packaging density and reduced travel distance This end-to-end optimization is not just an internal milestone; it has broad industry implications. As reported by Grocery Doppio, inefficient inventory visibility costs the grocery sector $7.4 billion annually. Amazon’s approach, anchored in regionalized fulfillment and data-driven inventory placement, offers a model of how to close these costly gaps.

In addition to the shelf-stable products and household goods available on Amazon.com, Amazon has innovated and invested significantly over the past decade to deliver best-in-class selection, low prices, and convenience to make it fast, easy, and affordable for customers to shop groceries through Amazon. Tens of millions of customers turn to Amazon Fresh and Whole Foods Market for their full-service grocery needs. And, customers in more than 3,500 cities and towns across the U.S. can use the Amazon website or mobile app to shop groceries across Whole Foods Market, Amazon Fresh, and local grocery and specialty retailers at great prices for convenient delivery and pickup. And, Prime members get unlimited grocery delivery on orders over $35 with a $9.99 monthly or $99.99 yearly grocery delivery subscription—a benefit that pays for itself in as little as one delivery order per month.

We know customers love having choice for their groceries depending on the occasion they’re shopping for, so we are also testing new experiences that make it easier for customers to shop expanded selection in one place. This includes 1) co-locating selection from Whole Foods Market, Amazon.com, and Amazon Fresh in the same fulfilment center enabling customers to shop items from all three brands and have them delivered in a single order, 2) opening a small-format grocery store under the same roof as Whole Foods Market in Chicago, letting customers shop their favorite natural and organic products at Whole Foods Market and getting a broader product assortment from Amazon in one trip, and 3) launching Whole Foods Market Daily Shop, a quick-shop store format that is fast and convenient when out and about. Read more about the [ways we’re making grocery shopping faster and easier](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-grocery-shopping-convenience-savings).

Amazon is one of the largest grocers in the U.S., with over $100B in gross sales—even when you exclude sales from [Whole Foods Market](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-grocery-delivery-subscription-prime-member-ebt-customers) and [Amazon Fresh](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-expands-grocery-delivery-and-pickup). But how did we get here? Over two decades ago, we started adding [groceries](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/groceries)and everyday household essentials to Amazon.com that don't require temperature control—items like bulk paper, cleaning products, large packs of canned and boxed food, and bottled drinks. Customers in big cities and rural communities alike loved the convenience of buying these items online and having them delivered quickly. So, over time we’ve lowered our cost-to-serve to cost-effectively add smaller packs of the most-purchased items, and broader selection of low-priced items.

*   Delivered at fastest speeds ever for Prime members globally in 2025. *   Continued increasing speed for rural customers in the U.S., with the average number of monthly customers receiving same-day delivery in rural areas nearly doubling year-over-year. *   Delivered nearly 70% more items same day in the U.S. than the year before, with Same-Day Delivery used by nearly 100 million customers. *   Expanded Amazon Now ultra-fast delivery, which offers delivery on thousands of items in 30 minutes or less. Amazon Now is now available in various cities in India, Mexico, and the UAE, and is being tested in several communities in the U.S. and UK. *   Expanded Same-Day grocery delivery to 2,300+ cities and towns across the U.S., making fresh groceries more accessible and transforming how customers shop for food, with perishables making up 9 of the top 10 most-ordered items in areas where the service is available.

A modern retail [order management system](https://www.weareplanet.com/order-management-system) centralizes inventory across channels, enables BOPIS and ship-from-store, and routes orders to the optimal location – reducing handling time and improving delivery accuracy.
Ever wonder what happens after a customer clicks “**BUY**” on your site or any e-commerce site for that matter?

![Image 1: Order processing times](https://cdn.amzprep.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Order-Processing-Times-1024x576.jpg)
Here’s a peek into the process: as soon as the order is confirmed, it triggers a sequence of events known as ecommerce order processing, a system that has to balance speed, accuracy, and cost simultaneously.

Every step has to ensure speed and accuracy. On top of that your customer has to get their order on time and in perfect condition. What goes on behind the scenes is more than just a simple click of the Buy button.

1. **Shipping Delays:**The pandemic disrupted global supply chains, leading to longer delivery times for many online orders. BOPIS became a way to circumvent these delays, offering customers faster access to their purchases. 2. **Evolving Customer Expectations:**Modern consumers value convenience. The ability to seamlessly integrate online browsing with in-store pickup caters to the desire for a fast and efficient shopping experience. A BOPIS system bridges this gap, giving consumers the immediacy of in-store shopping with a vast choice of online catalogs. 3. **Distribution center logistics:** Many centers — perhaps even most — weren’t prepared for the surge in [order fulfillment](https://www.deckcommerce.com/blog/what-is-order-fulfillment) needs. They’ve struggled to gain their footing, establish new workflows, and run smoothly. 4. **Reduced Carbon Footprint:**BOPIS can lead to fewer delivery trucks on the road, especially if consumers pick up items while running other errands.

_Retailer story:_[Target](https://www.barilliance.com/click-collect/#tab-con-4)’s got this on lock, advertising a typical two-hour fulfillment. Although they’ve offered order pickup for years, they’ve seen major growth, attributable to BOPIS investments, during the pandemic. In-store pickup has gone up 60%, with overall same-day fulfillment (BOPIS and curbside) increasing by a combined 273%.

*   **Extended sale deadlines:** Whereas shipping means cutoff dates — such as needing to place your order by Dec. 10 to ensure delivery by Christmas — retailers can still drive people to their storefront and continue to push promotional messages up until the big day. *   **Optimize real estate investment:** If foot traffic is down, BOPIS can supplement sales to ensure retailers are getting the most out of their real estate investment. In this way, BOPIS was key during lockdowns, when many brands could no longer afford their retail space. Some retail giants — like J.C. Penney and Neiman Marcus — were [forced into bankruptcy](https://retalon.com/blog/bopis-for-retail). *   **Volume stabilization:**Allocating inventory to local stores spreads out the volume from ecommerce orders, putting less of a stress on those overwhelmed warehouses. *   **Optimize the final mile:**Since the consumer is picking up their order, companies save on last mile costs with BOPIS ‘shipping’.

*   **Hybrid convenience:** If you forgot to add a product to your online cart, you can easily pick it up while at the store retrieving the rest of your order. ([75% of past BOPIS users](https://www.invespcro.com/blog/buy-online-pick-up-in-store-bopis/) say they’re likely to make another purchase while in the store.) Or, ask a sales associate in person any questions you have about your purchase. It’s a hybrid experience of online shopping and a traditional retail service.
**Retailer story:**[One little trick](https://thekrazycouponlady.com/tips/store-hacks/22-bath-body-works-hacks-thatll-literally-blow-your-mind) for getting the most out of [Bath & Body Works](https://www.bathandbodyworks.com/s/BathAndBodyWorks/order-pickup)’ online sales is by placing the order online and then selecting Pick Up in Store. (Not all locations offer online order pickup.)

*   **Increase in profitability**: When considering the cost of fulfillment and shipping, this is an easy takeaway – the retailer in this case is saving on the packing materials and labor or covering the cost of shipping fees. *   **Heightened foot traffic**: BOPIS brings customers into the store who may typically shop online, and once they’re in the store, [49% of US shoppers made additional purchases while picking up their BOPIS item](https://www.openpr.com/news/2360689/bopis-statistics-2021-industry-research-market-share-trend). *   **Improvement in customer satisfaction**: With increases in shipping times, BOPIS poses a quicker option for receiving items, if customers need their product sooner than the available shipping option. *   **Lower rates of returns**: Items picked up in-store results in fewer returns (although also easier and more cost-effective returns than the contrary shipping return process).

Buy online pickup in store (BOPIS) allows customers to place an order from a retailer’s website and pick it up at their closest store location. This option saves customers time and money on shipping, and quicker gratification with fast fulfillment on items they need sooner.
![Image 6: BOPIS from Amz](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6478b51cb2a3f3f4ad8c3748/64b51425d97c954b4ae34aa9_BOPIS%2520from%2520Amz.png)
The BOPIS strategy is a great option for retailers who have both a storefront as well as an ecommerce store.

raw_passages.text: Store pages contain customizable sections of tiles. Each tile can include content such as text, images, videos, and products.
Every Store page has a header section built in and needs to have at least 1 additional content tile.

*   4 background video tiles
*   1 product grid tile
*   1 gallery tile
*   1 featured deals tile
*   1 recommended products tile

If you reach the limit of one of these tile types, you won’t be able to add another unless you delete an existing tile of that type. Alternatively, you can change the content in any existing tile of that type.

**The Skinny:**_Amazon Stores are free, self-managed tools that allow brand owners to create a customized, multi-page shopping experience to build brand equity and showcase their full product catalog. By leveraging creative modules like shoppable images, video backgrounds, and intuitive navigation, brands can improve aesthetics and drive both on- and off-platform traffic to increase Marketplace success._

Amazon Stores allow brand owners to design and create multipage stores to showcase their brands, products, and value proposition on Amazon. Long gone are the days when Amazon sellers didn’t have the tools they needed to [build brand equity](https://tinuiti.com/blog/measurement/brand-equity-and-its-impact-on-revenue/) and promote shopper loyalty.
![Image 1](https://tinuiti.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/tinuiti-team-author-purple-1-150x150.png)

Once launched, Amazon Stores quickly shifted from being a trending Amazon feature to becoming a brand essential for [Marketplace success](https://tinuiti.com/our-work/#amazon). Not only do the creative features of Stores help to improve the aesthetics of brands on the Amazon Marketplace—they also provide new opportunities to drive traffic (on and off Amazon) to a brand’s entire catalog.

Amazon is pulling the plug on its high‑tech grocery experiment, announcing plans to shutter 23 Amazon Fresh and Amazon Go stores across California, part of a sweeping nationwide retreat from the cashier‑free model the tech giant once touted as the future of shopping. An Amazon spokesperson confirmed that 57 Amazon Go stores and 15 Amazon Fresh locations will close nationwide. California’s closures will come later than others because grocery stores must give a 45‑day notice under state law. Employees will be offered new roles or severance. Amazon says it will continue its Fresh online grocery operations, even as its physical ambitions downshift. Some of the soon‑to‑close locations may eventually reopen as Whole Foods Market stores — a chain the company purchased in 2017 — though Amazon declined to identify which addresses may be converted. Here's what to know about Amazon Fresh.

Company says it 'hasn’t found the right economic model' In announcing the shutdowns on Tuesday, Amazon said it had not achieved “a truly distinctive customer experience with the right economic model needed for large‑scale expansion.” Amazon Fresh launched as a delivery‑only service in 2007 and expanded into brick‑and‑mortar stores in 2020 in Los Angeles and Chicago. Amazon Go — smaller-format stores featuring cashier‑less checkout — debuted in Seattle and later expanded to Los Angeles County. Both chains leaned heavily on Amazon’s “just walk out” concept and Dash Carts, which tallied items in real time and charged shoppers automatically. But despite the initial buzz, Amazon struggled to grow the concept beyond early adopters and high‑traffic urban areas. Rancho Mirage Fresh store won’t open after all The news marks the final chapter for the long‑anticipated Amazon Fresh store in Rancho Mirage , which has sat in limbo for years.

The lime‑green signage first went up in 2022 at the Rancho Las Palmas shopping center off Bob Hope Drive. City officials said as recently as last year that Amazon was still paying rent and intended to open. But the company’s announcement on Tuesday closes the door. The 10,000‑square‑foot building — renovated after Stein Mart’s 2020 bankruptcy — has remained empty through multiple waves of speculation. With Whole Foods sitting just a mile away in Palm Desert, it’s unclear whether Amazon would consider a second location nearby. A city spokesperson told The Desert Sun that Rancho Mirage has received no new information. The center’s owner, AlbaneseCormier, did not respond to requests for comment. What Amazon plans next: More Whole Foods, more delivery While Amazon is winding down its Fresh and Go footprint, the company says it is gearing up for a major Whole Foods expansion — more than 100 new locations over the next few years, including compact Whole Foods Market Daily Shop stores.

It remains unclear whether any of those stores will be in California or whether former Fresh or Go sites are under consideration. What is clear is that Amazon is leaning harder into convenience and logistics. The company says perishable grocery purchases through its Same‑Day Delivery service have grown 40× since January 2025, and fresh foods now make up nine of the 10 most‑ordered items in areas where the service is available.

Amazon is one of the most recognisable brands in the world, and the third largest by revenue. It was the fourth tech company to reach a $1 trillion market cap, and a market leader in e-commerce, cloud, advertising, video streaming, and music streaming.

Originally launched as an online bookstore in 1995, Amazon spent its first few years as a brokerage for other sellers, similar to eBay. However, founder Jeff Bezos always [envisioned](https://www.businessinsider.com/jeff-bezos-amazon-history-facts-2017-4?r=US&IR=T) it would be an “everything store” and quickly added other items to the e-commerce platform.

As Amazon’s e-commerce platform continued to grow, Amazon looked for new ways to generate revenue. It launched the Kindle, an e-reader, in 2007, as the primary hardware for its Kindle e-book store. It also launched tablets and connected TV devices, under the Fire brand.

While Amazon still makes a majority of its revenue from its e-commerce platform, it has seen huge increases in revenue from AWS, subscriptions and advertising in the past few years. The coronavirus pandemic provided Amazon with a boost in sales across the board.
**Highlights.**Amazon Prime memberships total over **200 million** worldwide; _180.1 million_ members are in the U.S.

*   Amazon revenue from Prime memberships totaled **$44.374 billion**, representing _6.96%_ of the company’s 2024 revenue ($637.959 billion).
*   Amazon Prime Video has a **22%** share of the video streaming market; comparatively, Netflix has a _21%_ share.
*   One year of Amazon Prime membership costs **$139**.
*   Prime members spend an average of **$1,170**per year on Amazon.
*   During Prime Day alone, Amazon Prime members spent **$24.1 billion**.

In addition to understanding the target market, a unique value proposition is crucial for a successful go-to-market strategy. A value proposition is a clear statement that explains how a company's products or services solve a specific problem or provide a unique benefit to customers. It communicates the value that customers can expect to receive by choosing the company's offerings over competitors. A strong value proposition not only attracts customers but also helps build brand loyalty and advocacy.

Moreover, a well-defined go-to-market strategy enables a company to differentiate itself from competitors. In a crowded marketplace, where customers are bombarded with countless options, a unique value proposition sets a company apart and convinces customers to choose their products or services over others. It highlights the specific benefits and advantages that the company's offerings provide, giving customers a compelling reason to buy.

In conclusion, a well-executed go-to-market strategy is essential for companies to effectively bring their products or services to market and connect with customers. By understanding the target market, developing a unique value proposition, and selecting the right distribution channels, companies can differentiate themselves, create value for customers, and drive sales and revenue. It is a dynamic and ever-evolving process that requires continuous analysis, adaptation, and innovation to stay ahead in the competitive business landscape.

By Best Buy May 14, 2024 Next time you open the Best Buy® app , it might look a bit different. In the coming weeks, we’re rolling out new features designed to give customers a personalized shopping experience that’s as unique as they are. And one of the coolest parts is that each time you open the app, your experience will become more tailored and relevant. And even better, we‘ll be adding more and more proactive alerts to enhance every step of your technology journey with Best Buy. These new experiences will help unlock your imagination and inspire you to find technology that can elevate the world in ways you never thought possible. By continuing to leverage technologies including AI , we’ve personalized our app and put you in the driver’s seat, allowing you to shop and see products, categories and services the way you want.

For customers with a My Best Buy Plus™ or My Best Buy Total™ membership, you’ll also be able to enjoy an even more personalized experience while shopping within the app, including exclusive member deals and personalized offers. As a Plus or Total member, we’ll even send you push notifications to alert you on relevant deals, help you understand all the benefits of your membership, and even to celebrate and track how much money you’ve saved by taking advantage of your exclusive offers. “These enhancements to our app are further examples of how we’re continuing to leverage data and technology to personalize and humanize consumer electronics like nobody else can,” said Brian Tilzer, chief data, analytics and technology officer at Best Buy.

“Our customers have unique needs and preferences, and our goal is to inspire discovery of amazing new technology and ensure it truly enriches their lives, all in the most relevant, seamless way possible.” Here are more new experiences coming to your Best Buy app soon: Experience a more p ersonalized home screen Your home screen will be powered by AI and will deliver a distinct and engaging shopping experience based on what you are most interested in and where you are in your technology journey. This means each customer’s app home screen will look different, because it’s based on your personal preferences and other factors like shopping history, membership status and what we know you care about most. On a year-to-date basis, the company has returned a total of $802 million to shareholders through dividends of $602 million and share repurchases of $200 million. The company still expects to spend approximately $300 million on share repurchases during FY26.

During Q3 FY26, the company recorded pre-tax non-cash asset impairments of $192 million related to Best Buy Health, comprised of $171 million of goodwill and intangible asset impairments and $21 million of long-lived asset impairments. A change in Best Buy Health’s customer base during the quarter resulted in an impairment review of all Best Buy Health assets. The impairments reflect downward revisions in the company’s longer-term projections in part due to pressures in the Medicaid and Medicare Advantage markets.

By the end of 2023, Best Buy boasted a staggering $43.45 billion in total revenue. A significant portion, $18.674 million in FY 2023, came from e-commerce and online sales. This achievement underscores Best Buy’s mastery of the digital landscape, leveraging technology to expand its reach and deepen customer engagement. At the heart of Best Buy’s triumph lies its unwavering commitment to customer-centric practices. The company has crafted an engaging brand experience that resonates with consumers by seamlessly blending traditional marketing tactics with innovative digital initiatives. From captivating advertisements to interactive social media campaigns, Best Buy consistently fosters meaningful connections with its audience, cultivating loyalty and brand advocacy.

*   **Margin Expansion via Services:** The Services segment, which accounted for 6.34% of FY25 revenue (or $2.63 billion), is the key to gross profit rate improvement. In Q3 FY25, the Domestic gross profit rate improved to 23.6%, largely driven by the better financial performance of the services category and membership offerings. *   **Omnichannel Efficiency:** The company uses its physical store network to support its digital sales, with online revenue comprising 31.4% of total Domestic revenue in Q3 FY25. This model allows for fast fulfillment options like in-store pickup, which keeps logistics costs down compared to pure-play e-commerce. *   **New High-Margin Streams:** Management is actively building new revenue sources, including a US-based Best Buy Marketplace (targeting mid-2025), which introduces high-margin commission revenue without inventory risk, and scaling its Best Buy Ads business, capturing a bigger share of vendor advertising dollars.

Best Buy's revenue streams are heavily weighted toward hardware, but the Services segment is the strategic growth engine, driving higher-margin, recurring revenue and customer stickiness. For fiscal year 2025, the Services segment generated approximately **$2.63 billion** in revenue.

*   **Revenue and Sales Decline:** Total revenue for fiscal year 2025 was $41.53 billion, representing a 4.43% decline from the prior year. Full-year comparable sales are expected to decline between 2.5% and 3.5%. *   **Profitability Metrics:** Despite the revenue decline, the company has maintained a respectable Non-GAAP Operating Income rate, guided to be in the range of 4.1% to 4.2% for the full FY25. This shows strong operational efficiency in controlling Selling, General, and Administrative (SG&A) expenses. *   **Earnings Per Share (EPS):** The full-year Non-GAAP Diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS) is projected to be between $6.10 and $6.25. This is a critical metric showing the company's ability to generate value for shareholders even during a period of contracting top-line sales. *   **Capital Allocation:** Best Buy continues to return capital to shareholders, expecting to spend approximately $500 million on share repurchases during FY25, alongside its dividend payments.

*   **Service-Led Margin Expansion:** The company's focus on services, including the membership program, drove an improved gross profit rate of **22.6%** in FY25, even as revenue declined.
*   **Physical Footprint Optimization:** Management plans to close 10 to 15 stores in FY25 while testing small-format locations to capture share in underserved markets, maximizing physical store retention through convenience.
*   **New Revenue Streams:** The launch of Best Buy Marketplace and Best Buy Ads are crucial, high-execution-risk initiatives designed to create new, scalable profit streams and diversify revenue beyond product sales.
*   **Tariff De-Risking:** The company is actively reducing its exposure to China-related tariffs, with exposure decreasing to **30%-35%** from a previous high of 55%.

Best Buy's primary revenue comes from selling consumer electronics, but its services segment is a growing contributor. The company aims to diversify its income through recurring revenue and value-added services, adapting its monetization strategies to evolving consumer habits.

*   The Best Buy business model integrates both online and offline sales channels.
*   Best Buy's supply chain is designed for efficient product movement from manufacturers to consumers.
*   Customer engagement strategies include loyalty programs and the personalized services offered by Geek Squad.
*   The company competes with online retailers by leveraging its in-store experience and immediate product availability.
*   Best Buy's organizational hierarchy supports its diverse retail operations and strategic initiatives.
*   The [Revenue Streams & Business Model of Best Buy](https://pestel-analysis.com/blogs/owners/bestbuy) includes product sales, services, and membership offerings.

Consumer electronics and related products form the core of Best Buy's revenue. In fiscal year 2025, the company reported total revenue of $41.53 billion, a slight decrease from $43.45 billion in fiscal year 2024.

Best Buy is actively evolving its monetization strategies to include more recurring revenue and enhance customer loyalty. This shift is evident in the growth of its membership programs and the integration of services into its core offerings, reflecting a broader [Marketing Strategy of Best Buy](https://pestel-analysis.com/blogs/marketing-strategy/bestbuy).

Best Buy offers a paid My Best Buy Plus membership for $49.99 per year.
The My Best Buy Plus membership includes free 2-day shipping, exclusive member prices, deals, offers on thousands of items, and exclusive access to sales, events, and products.
The My Best Buy Total membership includes free 2-day shipping, exclusive member prices and access, and 24/7 access to Geek Squad Agents for support.
The free My Best Buy membership does not include free 2-day shipping, exclusive member prices, deals, offers, or exclusive access to sales and events.
Best Buy charges $39.99 for an in-store PC or tablet setup service by Geek Squad.
Best Buy charges $149.99 for a virus removal and operating system repair service.
Best Buy offers a Geek Squad two-year laptop protection plan for $189.99.
Geek Squad Protection plans for cell phones or gaming can be purchased as monthly installment payments for the duration of a contract.

However, as rates have peaked and started to decline in several key markets, and deposit behaviors have changed, net interest income is projected to grow more slowly, at about 2 percent per year through 2029, assuming no major disruptions. Meanwhile, growth in transaction-based revenue is expected to slow as consumers increasingly use lower-cost payment options like account-to-account transfers and digital wallets. At the same time, ongoing pricing pressures, especially within card-based ecosystems, combined with regulatory scrutiny and the rise of platform-driven payment experiences, are squeezing fee-based revenue models. Accordingly, we expect revenue growth to continue growing at 4 percent annually through 2029 (Exhibit 1). That number may range from as little as 3 percent in the case of global disruptions to as much as 6 percent with accelerated productivity improvements. At a growth rate of 4 percent, the total market size will reach $3.0 trillion by 2029.

Against this backdrop, the payments industry remains the most valuable part of financial services, generating $2.5 trillion in revenue from $2.0 quadrillion in value flows, supported by 3.6 trillion transactions worldwide.1 The _2025 McKinsey Global Payments Report_ offers insights into the future of the sector and what is needed to remain competitive in a rapidly changing environment. The report is based on analyses of McKinsey’s Global Payments Map, which includes data from 50 countries, more than two dozen payment methods, and accounts for 95 percent of global GDP. It is organized into three sections:

1.   A baseline forecast for industry growth through 2029, including a detailed examination of how economic volatility and policy changes are creating sharply divergent scenarios for margins and revenue mix.
2.   Major forces reshaping the payments landscape, including the monetization of AI-native operations and agentic commerce, new models of programmable liquidity, and regulated digital money.
3.   Investment priorities for operators navigating a transitioning system, focusing on agility, architecture, and trust.

From 2019 to 2024, global payments revenue increased on average by 7 percent annually. Interest income made up 46 percent of total revenues in 2024, supported by higher rates. In 2024, payments revenue growth slowed to 4 percent, a notable drop from the 12 percent increase in 2023. This deceleration was caused by peaking interest rates, a more muted macroeconomic environment, structural changes toward lower-yield payment methods, and ongoing fee pressures. Regionally, Latin America grew by 11 percent, while Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) and North America increased by 8 percent and 5 percent, respectively, and Asia–Pacific (APAC) shrank by 1 percent. Nonetheless, payments is still the most valuable subsector in finance. In 2024, payments gave an average 18.9 percent return on equity, with some players earning more than 100 percent.2

Understanding the **customer demographics Best Buy** serves is crucial for grasping its market position. The company primarily focuses on the business-to-consumer (B2C) market, although it also caters to businesses through its business-to-business (B2B) segment. This dual approach allows for a broad reach, adapting to various consumer needs and preferences.

Best Buy's ability to adapt to changing consumer preferences and technological advancements has been key to its success. The company's emphasis on services, such as Geek Squad, has broadened its appeal to a wider audience that values convenience and problem-solving. For more insights into the company's history and evolution, see the [Brief History of Best Buy](https://swottemplate.com/blogs/brief-history/bestbuy-brief-history). As of 2024, Best Buy continues to refine its strategies to meet the evolving needs of its diverse customer base, ensuring its position in the competitive consumer electronics market. Recent financial reports show a steady revenue stream, reflecting the company's ability to maintain its relevance and adapt to market changes. The consumer segment remains the largest revenue generator, with services and total home solutions playing an increasingly important role.

*   **Product Quality and Reliability:** Customers seek high-quality, reliable products with a strong brand reputation.
*   **Price and Value:** Competitive pricing and perceived value are significant factors in purchasing decisions.
*   **Expert Advice and Support:** Customers value knowledgeable staff and access to technical support and services.
*   **Convenience:** Easy access to products, both in-store and online, along with convenient services like installation and setup, are essential.
*   **Latest Technology:** Customers desire access to the newest gadgets and technological advancements.
*   **Customer Service:** Positive experiences with customer service and post-purchase support are critical for customer satisfaction.

A key aspect of the company's strategy is its use of data and CRM systems to segment its audience. By analyzing customer data, the company personalizes marketing messages, offers relevant product recommendations, and provides promotions tailored to individual customer preferences. This targeted approach enhances the customer experience and increases the likelihood of repeat purchases, directly impacting the company's revenue streams, as detailed in [Revenue Streams & Business Model of Best Buy](https://swottemplate.com/blogs/how-it-works/bestbuy-how-it-works).

The Domestic segment generated 92.08% of total revenue in fiscal year 2025, with the International segment contributing 7.92%. The company is also expanding into the digital health market, a sector projected to reach $192 billion by 2025.

The company appeals to middle-class shoppers by offering value through sales and price matching. Family households are also a significant segment, with **33.4%** of households being married couples with children in 2024.

[Best Buy](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/BBY/) hiked its full-year forecast Tuesday, as it topped Wall Street's quarterly sales expectations and customers turned to the retailer to upgrade laptops and splurge on new gaming consoles and smartphones.

The consumer electronics retailer said it now expects revenue of between $41.65 billion to $41.95 billion for the full year, higher than its previous range of $41.1 billion to $41.9 billion. It expects adjusted earnings per share of $6.25 to $6.35, compared with its prior range of $6.15 to $6.30.

Best Buy said it expects full-year comparable sales, a metric that tracks sales online and at stores open at least 14 months, to range between a 0.5% rise to a 1.2% increase, compared with its previous expectations for a 1% decline and a 1% climb.

### Best Buy joins a growing trend of retailers using Uber Eats,Instacart and DoorDash to provide same-day delivery.

Best Buy joins a growing trend of retailers using[Uber Eats](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2025/05/06/mothers-day-1-800-flowers-uber-eats/),[Instacart](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2025/04/04/instacart-in-stock-status-for-inventory/)and[DoorDash](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2025/01/22/home-depot-adds-delivery-through-doordash-and-uber-eats/)to provide same-day delivery. Days before the announcement, Dollar Tree and Uber Eats announced a similar partnership, as did Merchants Distributors and Instacart.

“Bringing Dollar Tree to the Uber Eats platform means customers can now enjoy the great value and everyday essentials they count on, plus the thrill of discovering those unexpected treasures — all with the convenience of same-day delivery,” said Brent Beebe, senior vice president of retail merchandising and marketing at Dollar Tree, in a statement. “We’re making it easier than ever for our shoppers to access the fun, affordable finds they love, right when and where they need them.”
Even a wholesale grocery distributor, Merchants Distributors (MDI), is working with Instacart to offer same-day delivery. The companies announced their partnership Aug. 28 as well.

Best Buy, Macy's Expand Same-Day Delivery To Speed Holiday Sales
===============

Best Buy, Macy's Expand Same-Day Delivery To Speed Holiday Sales
================================================================
Best Buy and Macy's are expanding same-day delivery services in advance of the holiday season as it seems the battle for Christmas will be waged by one-hour delivery drivers.

Best Buy is tripling the number of metropolitan areas beginning next week with same-day delivery available in 27 metro areas. "We expect customers in nearly 40 cities to be eligible for the service by the holiday season," according to [a company statement](https://corporate.bestbuy.com/best-buy-expands-day-delivery-service/).

Best Buy first dipped its toes in same-day delivery last fall with a test in San Francisco in a partnership with Deliv, which uses a fleet of independent contractors as drivers. It added New York City to the program earlier this year. Then, late last month, it quietly rolled out same-day delivery to the other 11 markets where Deliv operates.

Daphne Carmeli, Deliv's chief executive, said electronics is one of the top categories for which customers place same-day delivery orders. Sometimes they are for last-minute gifts; other times it could be because someone loses a cellphone charger.

Meanwhile, Amazon has been stepping on the gas when it comes getting items to customers' doorsteps faster. On Wednesday, it announced it has nearly doubled the number of metro areas in the U.S. that can now receive free same-day delivery on orders placed through its Prime program.
Minneapolis-based Target Corp. has also been testing same-day delivery, or what it calls "rush delivery," in a handful of markets since 2014.

[Best Buy](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/BBY/) hiked its full-year forecast Tuesday, as it topped Wall Street's quarterly sales expectations and customers turned to the retailer to upgrade laptops and splurge on new gaming consoles and smartphones.

The consumer electronics retailer said it now expects revenue of between $41.65 billion to $41.95 billion for the full year, higher than its previous range of $41.1 billion to $41.9 billion. It expects adjusted earnings per share of $6.25 to $6.35, compared with its prior range of $6.15 to $6.30.

Best Buy said it expects full-year comparable sales, a metric that tracks sales online and at stores open at least 14 months, to range between a 0.5% rise to a 1.2% increase, compared with its previous expectations for a 1% decline and a 1% climb.

*   It joins a growing trend of retailers who are using third-party sellers as a way to attract sales, drive higher profits and draw advertising dollars.
*   The consumer electronics retailer's business could use a boost as it contends with higher tariffs, sluggish housing turnover and consumers' selective spending.

The company's online marketplace riffs off those of other retailers, such as [Amazon](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AMZN/) and [Walmart](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/WMT/), by relying on third-party sellers to stock, sell and ship inventory and taking a cut of their sales in the form of a commission.

Best Buy’s third-party marketplace isn’t just growing—it’s accelerating. In 2025, third-party GMV crossed $3.03 billion, up 35% year-over-year. By 2026, analysts project $4.1 billion in third-party sales—accounting for nearly 22% of total company revenue. This isn’t a side channel; it’s a strategic growth engine for brands that understand how Best Buy’s ecosystem differs from Amazon or Walmart Marketplace. Unlike broad-appeal platforms, Best Buy rewards precision: deep category expertise, technical credibility, post-purchase support readiness, and alignment with its “Tech Concierge” customer promise. Sellers who treat Best Buy as a premium retail extension—not just another listing venue—capture disproportionate share. This article distills what works *now*, based on verified seller performance data, platform policy shifts effective January 2026, and insights from top-performing vendors who’ve grown 3–5x faster than the marketplace average.

Best Buy’s marketplace operates under a hybrid model: first-party inventory sets price benchmarks and delivery expectations, while third-party sellers must meet or exceed those standards to earn visibility. Its shoppers aren’t browsing casually—they’re researching high-intent purchases: home theater setups, smart home ecosystems, gaming peripherals, and business-grade audio/video gear. Average order value (AOV) on Best Buy is $287—nearly double Amazon’s ($152)—and conversion rates for qualified listings exceed 8.3%, versus 2.1% industry average for electronics marketplaces. But access isn’t automatic. Best Buy enforces strict vendor qualification: minimum $1M annual revenue, documented warranty service capability, and adherence to its “Tech Certified” badge requirements—including product-specific setup guides, video demos, and live chat support during peak hours.

facts.claim: Best Buy moves to curbside pickup only as it sees surge in orders for home office equipment.
Curbside Pickup is not available at all stores; customers must confirm availability by looking for 'Eligible for Best Buy Curbside Pickup' designation.
Curbside Pickup supports pedestrians and cyclists, and customers can check in using smartphone via email, text message, or Best Buy mobile app.
Customers can designate someone else to pick up Curbside Pickup orders, and the pickup person needs a 4-digit code and may be asked for ID.
Curbside Pickup items are held at the store for 5 days; if not picked up, the order is cancelled and refunded.
Curbside Pickup is contactless, fast, easy, and free, available on eligible products at most store locations.
For Curbside Pickup, customers select 'Use Curbside Pickup' during checkout and receive an email when the order is ready.
Upon arrival for Curbside Pickup, customers check in via app or other methods, and employees bring items to the car.
For Store Pickup, customers head inside to the Order Pickup sign where an employee assists.
Best Buy is opening doors at midnight for the Switch 2 launch for customers to pick up consoles.
Curbside Pickup instructions are available in the Best Buy mobile app for check-in.

Yes. Customers can modify Curbside Pickup orders. For example, you may switch to a different store location. However, Curbside Pickup is not available at all stores; so, you’ll need to confirm that Curbside Pickup is available at the store location you’ve selected, by looking for the “Eligible for Best Buy Curbside Pickup” designation when modifying your order. If the store you select does not offer Curbside Pickup, you may switch to our Store Pickup option, but you'll have to come inside the store to pick up your order. You may also modify your order to have it shipped to your home or another address.

Yes. Curbside Pickup supports pedestrians and cyclists. When you arrive at the store, go near the entrance and use your smartphone to click on the “How to Check in at Curbside” button in the “Your Order Is Ready for Pickup” confirmation email, click on the link in the “Your Order Is Ready” text message, or click on “Curbside Pickup Instructions” in the Best Buy mobile app. You’ll be prompted to provide information about how we can identify you and where you are located when you check in. You can describe what you’re wearing and where you’re standing, and an employee will be with you shortly. If you do not have a smartphone, see below for alternate instructions.

You may drive up to pick up your order yourself or choose someone else to pick it up. To have your order picked up by someone else,select that option during checkout. You’ll be asked to provide the pickup person’s name, email address and phone number. Your designated pickup person will be asked for the 4-digit code that is generated when checking in upon arrival to the pickup location. An ID may be requested upon pickup. Only you — or the person you’ve told us will pick up your order — can pick up your items. To change the person picking up your order, go to your order details and select Make Changes.
Yes. You may cancel at any time. We’ll hold your Curbside Pickup items at the store for 5 days. If you don’t pick up your items by then, we’ll cancel the order and refund your method of payment.

facts.claim: Best Buy introduced a small-format, digital-first store concept in 2022 in Charlotte, North Carolina.
The small-format store in Charlotte is 5,000 square feet.
Best Buy has a deal with Bell Canada to rebrand and operate 165 small format consumer electronics stores previously known as The Source.
Best Buy is testing closing large stores and opening smaller ones in the same area.
Best Buy is expanding into new markets with no prior physical presence.

raw_passages.text: Bruce Bennett/Getty Images By Alex Vuocolo March 4, 2024 • less than 3 min read Best Buy is planning an experiment. In the next fiscal year, the electronics retailer will test its ability to retain its customer base by closing large stores and opening smaller ones in the same area. The company introduced its “ small-format, digital-first store ” concept back in 2022 in Charlotte, North Carolina. The 5,000 square-foot location promised a “curated selection” of products, Geek Squad services, and scan-and-go capabilities. Relatedly, Best Buy recently struck a deal with Bell Canada to rebrand and operate 165 small format consumer electronics stores previously known as The Source. Best Buy will provide the products and the supply chain, marketing, and e-commerce expertise, while Bell will offer telecommunications services and operate the stores. The embrace of small format is just the latest instance of Best Buy’s efforts to reimagine its physical footprint.

unique_value_proposition.full_report_markdown:
# Comparative Analysis: Unique Value Propositions Across Five Major U.S. Retailers

## 1. The Landscape: Five Promises, One Consumer Wallet

The five largest U.S. general-merchandise and specialty retailers each anchor their brand around a distinct core promise. Understanding how these promises overlap, diverge, and evolve reveals where competitive advantage is durable and where white space remains for new positioning.

## 2. Company-by-Company UVP Assessment

### Walmart — "Save Money. Live Better."
Walmart's value proposition is the most literal and the most scalable. The company describes itself as "people-led, tech-powered" and frames its mission around delivering "value, a broad assortment of quality items and services, a convenient and enjoyable shopping experience, and to do business with a company they trust" [S2]. Its EDLP philosophy is not merely a pricing tactic but a structural commitment: Walmart's cost-leadership model—anchored by 4,700+ U.S. stores and an expanding e-commerce platform—makes it the gravitational center of value retailing [S5].

Critically, Walmart is now layering AI-driven personalization on top of its price foundation. Its GenAI-powered shopping assistant is "trained on Walmart data, enabling us to combine it with other LLMs to create responses and complete tasks that are highly contextual and tailored to the customer's specific needs" [S1]. Its Trend-to-Product pipeline uses generative AI to shorten product development cycles, signaling an ambition to add curation and discovery to its historically utilitarian brand [S1]. This is a direct incursion into Target's territory.

**Verdict:** Walmart's UVP is the broadest and most defensible on price, but its emotional resonance remains low. The AI push is an attempt to close that gap.

### Target — "Expect More. Pay Less."
Target occupies the most emotionally charged position in this set. CEO Brian Cornell frames the brand around "differentiated options and distinctive shopping experiences without sacrificing value" [S1]. Target's owned-brand portfolio (over 45 brands including Cat & Jack, Good & Gather, Threshold) and high-profile designer partnerships (Champion, Diane von Furstenberg, etc.) are its primary moat [S1, S7]. The company is "reimagining key categories" such as gaming, sports, and toys with expanded assortments and enhanced in-store experiences [S1].

Target's strategic vulnerability is that its dual promise—style *and* value—is under pressure from both flanks. Walmart's AI-enabled curation threatens to narrow the style gap, while Amazon's same-day delivery erodes Target's convenience claims. Target's response is to lean harder into discovery: "reinforcing Target as the destination for discovery by further blending its one-of-a-kind physical, digital and social commerce shopping experiences" [S1]. The company's community giving (5% of profits since 1946) adds a purpose dimension that competitors match less consistently [S4].

**Verdict:** Target's UVP is the most emotionally differentiated but also the most fragile, sitting in a contested middle ground.

### Costco — "The Membership That Pays for Itself"
Costco's value proposition is structurally unique among the five. Its business model has been compared to Netflix's rather than Walmart's: membership fees fund operations, allowing the company to sell goods at near-zero margin [S7]. The company carries roughly 3,800 SKUs versus Walmart's ~140,000, creating a curated, high-quality assortment where "they pick a few vendors, all higher quality ones" with "unique, higher volume packaging" [S1]. This limited selection, combined with rotating inventory, produces the "treasure hunt" psychology that drives repeat visits [S4, S8].

Costco's Code of Ethics explicitly ties its mission to four pillars: obey the law, take care of members, take care of employees, and respect suppliers [S5]. The Kirkland Signature private label—spanning everything from olive oil to golf balls—reinforces the trust proposition: members believe Costco has pre-vetted quality on their behalf.

Analysts highlight Costco's "unique retail model and solid growth" as standing out even in challenging markets [S3]. With membership renewal rates consistently above 90%, the model is self-reinforcing and extremely difficult to replicate.

**Verdict:** Costco's UVP is the most defensible and the hardest to imitate. Its weakness is limited digital sophistication and a narrow demographic appeal (higher-income, bulk-buying households).

### Amazon — "Earth's Most Customer-Centric Company"
Amazon's stated principles are "customer obsession rather than competitor focus, passion for invention, commitment to operational excellence, and long-term thinking" [S1]. Its UVP is the convergence of three factors: price competitiveness, speed of delivery, and virtually unlimited selection [S4]. Prime membership bundles these into a sticky ecosystem that includes video, music, and grocery delivery.

Amazon's advantage is structural: its logistics network, marketplace model, and AWS-funded R&D create a flywheel that competitors cannot match on breadth. However, Amazon's weakness is the absence of emotional discovery or curation. Shopping on Amazon is efficient but rarely delightful. The platform optimizes for "I know what I want" purchases rather than "show me something I didn't know I needed."

Andy Jassy's 2024 shareholder letter [S9] emphasizes continued investment in delivery speed and AI-powered recommendations, suggesting Amazon sees personalization as the path to adding discovery without sacrificing efficiency.

**Verdict:** Amazon's UVP is the broadest moat in retail but the least emotionally engaging. It wins on need-based purchases and loses on want-based discovery.

### Best Buy — "Enriching Lives Through Technology"
Best Buy's UVP is the most specialized. The company positions itself as the place where technology expertise meets retail: "competitive pricing, extensive product selection, and knowledgeable staff, creating an unmatched shopping experience" [S3]. Geek Squad, celebrating 30 years [S2], is the tangible embodiment of this promise—an in-home and in-store service capability that no competitor matches at scale.

However, Best Buy acknowledges that its role is evolving: "Our customers... don't always need us to be the expert anymore. Customers are more familiar with technology, do a tremendous amount of research on their own" [S1]. The company is pivoting from transactional expertise to relationship-based personalization, rolling out AI-powered app features and a "Discover tab where customers can explore new tech" [S1]. VP of Customer Strategy April Wagner frames this as a shift toward "customer obsession," noting that Best Buy was historically "very transactional in nature" [S4].

**Verdict:** Best Buy's UVP is the most differentiated in its category but faces secular headwinds as consumer tech literacy rises and AI-assisted shopping reduces the need for human expertise.

## 3. Competitive Dynamics and Convergence

Three convergence vectors are reshaping the landscape:

1. **AI-Powered Personalization as Universal Ambition:** Walmart [S1], Amazon [S9], and Best Buy [S1] are all investing heavily in GenAI shopping assistants. This threatens to commoditize the "curation" and "expertise" claims that differentiate Target and Best Buy respectively.

2. **Membership Models Gaining Ground:** Costco's membership model [S7] and Amazon Prime represent closed-loop ecosystems that generate recurring revenue and behavioral lock-in. Walmart+ is an explicit response. Target lacks a comparable membership tier, which may become a strategic liability.

3. **Physical-Digital Blending:** Target's Drive Up and store-as-hub model [S1], Walmart's omnichannel push [S8], and Best Buy's app-driven personalization [S1] all reflect the reality that pure-play digital (Amazon) and pure-play physical (legacy Costco) are converging toward hybrid models.

## 4. Winners, Losers, and the Contested Middle

**Winner:** Costco's structural differentiation—membership-funded low margins, limited SKU curation, treasure-hunt psychology—is the hardest to replicate and the least threatened by AI or e-commerce convergence.

**Strong Position:** Amazon's convenience moat is nearly unassailable for need-based purchases, though it leaves emotional discovery to others.

**Under Pressure:** Target's "affordable style" positioning is the most contested, squeezed by Walmart's AI-enabled curation from below and Amazon's speed from above. Best Buy's expertise claim is eroding as consumers and AI become more capable.

## 5. White Space and Strategic Implications

The most significant unoccupied territory lies at the intersection of **expert curation + emotional discovery + transparent value**—a space where a retailer acts as a trusted advisor who surfaces surprising, high-quality products at fair prices with full transparency on sourcing and value. Costco approaches this but lacks digital sophistication. Target approaches it but lacks the trust mechanics of a membership model. No player fully owns it.
white_space: Digitally-native treasure hunt: No player combines Costco's curated surprise with Amazon's digital convenience — a membership-based, algorithmically-curated discovery platform for quality goods at transparent margins remains unoccupied.

Expert-guided lifestyle curation beyond electronics: Best Buy owns tech expertise but no retailer offers comparable human + AI advisory services for home, wellness, or sustainability categories at scale.

Value transparency as brand identity: None of the five leads with radical cost transparency (showing markup, sourcing costs, etc.) — a positioning that could appeal to trust-seeking younger consumers.

Community-embedded micro-curation: While Target invests in community giving [S4] and Walmart in local assortment, no player has built a UVP around hyper-local, community-curated product selection powered by local tastemakers.

Subscription-based replenishment + discovery hybrid: Amazon Subscribe & Save handles replenishment; Costco handles discovery; no player seamlessly blends automated restocking of essentials with curated surprise boxes of new products in a single membership.
trends: AI-powered personalization is becoming table stakes: Walmart, Amazon, and Best Buy are all deploying GenAI shopping assistants, threatening to commoditize curation and expertise as differentiators [Walmart S1, Best Buy S1, Amazon S9].

Membership and loyalty ecosystems are replacing one-time transactions: Costco, Amazon Prime, and Walmart+ reflect a structural shift toward recurring-revenue, behaviorally-locked consumer relationships.

Physical stores are being repositioned as experience and fulfillment hubs rather than inventory warehouses: Target's category reinvention [S1], Best Buy's app-integrated store experience [S1], and Walmart's omnichannel model [S8] all reflect this shift.

The 'expertise premium' is deflating: Best Buy explicitly acknowledges that customers 'don't always need us to be the expert anymore' [Best Buy S1], signaling that human expertise must be augmented or replaced by AI-assisted guidance.

Owned brands and private labels are becoming primary differentiation tools: Target's 45+ owned brands [S7] and Costco's Kirkland Signature are increasingly central to UVP defense against marketplace commoditization.

positioning.headline: Amazon dominates cross-tier positioning with unmatched breadth from mass-market to enterprise, while Walmart's aggressive upmarket push and Costco's affluent-value paradox are reshaping the competitive landscape—leaving a widening gap in premium specialty electronics and curated lifestyle segments.
positioning.executive_summary: The five major retailers occupy increasingly overlapping but distinct positioning tiers, with Amazon as the only player credibly spanning mass-market consumer, premium services, and enterprise segments simultaneously. Walmart's strategic pivot from pure value leader toward premium experiences creates both opportunity and identity risk, while Costco's unique membership model captures affluent consumers who paradoxically seek value. Target's 'affordable premium' niche and Best Buy's specialty electronics positioning face the greatest squeeze as competitors encroach from above and below, revealing critical white space in premium curated retail and integrated tech-lifestyle services.
